@graph.description: Can you make money from trading? Yes, some traders do — but SEBI's data says over 9 in 10 F&O traders lose money. Learn the expectancy math, position-sizing rules, and realistic monthly income figures before you risk capital.
@graph.headline: Can You Make Money From Trading? The Honest Answer, With the Math

acceptedAnswer.text: Beginners can make money on individual trades, but consistent profit is rare in the first year. The realistic beginner goal is a clean journal of 30 to 50 rule-following trades, from which expectancy can be computed. Most beginners lose money early because they risk too much per trade, trade without stops, and judge strategies on a handful of trades.

mainEntity.name: Can beginners make money from trading?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trading is a good way to make money only for people who treat it as a skill-based business with measurable edges and strict risk control. For everyone else, it is one of the fastest ways to lose money, as SEBI's data shows. It is a poor way to make urgent money; if you need income this month, a job or freelance work pays with certainty that trading cannot offer.

mainEntity.name: Is trading a good way to make money?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, some traders make a living from trading, but the conditions are demanding: a proven positive expectancy over many trades, capital large enough that a realistic monthly return covers expenses, and living expenses saved separately from trading capital. A practical test is six consecutive months where trading profits cover monthly expenses, with losing months absorbed without touching living savings.

mainEntity.name: Can you make a living from trading?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no honest single number, because monthly trading income depends on capital, expectancy, and market conditions. As arithmetic illustration only: 5,00,000 rupees of capital earning 2% a month produces about 10,000 rupees, while 10,00,000 rupees at the same rate produces about 20,000 rupees. Averages hide the fact that most traders lose money, so your own expectancy multiplied by your capital is the only monthly figure that means anything.

mainEntity.name: How much do traders earn per month?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Even consistently profitable traders have losing days and losing months. A trader averaging 2% a month can easily post a negative 3% month followed by a positive 8% month. Daily profit targets are dangerous because they pressure traders into taking trades their plan does not justify. Professionals judge results over quarters, not days.

mainEntity.name: Do traders make money every day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most traders lose money for a short list of repeatable reasons: they risk too much per trade, trade without stop-losses, overtrade out of boredom or revenge, ignore costs, and judge strategies on tiny samples. SEBI's data adds a structural reason: in leveraged futures and options, costs and leverage compound small mistakes into large losses, which is why over 91% of individual F&O traders lost money in FY2024-25.

mainEntity.name: Why do most traders lose money?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trading is better than a regular job only once it reliably pays more, with less stress, than the job it replaces — measured over at least six months of real records, not one good month. Before that point, a job is better in almost every way: fixed pay, benefits, and no risk of paying to work. The smartest arrangement for most people is both: a job for certainty and trading as a growing side skill.
